# Moonraker metadata

Fable Slicer emits the metadata comments print hosts parse — layer count,
time estimate, filament totals, heights, nozzle, filament identity, the
first-layer targets — in the PrusaSlicer/Orca spelling those hosts expect.
See `emit_host_metadata` in `engine/src/emit.rs`, and
`host_metadata_uses_the_field_names_hosts_parse` for the pinned list.

Whether Moonraker *reads* them depends on its version, because it picks a
metadata parser by sniffing the file's identity line.

## Our identity line

```
; generated by Fable Slicer 0.0.0 on 2026-08-18 at 22:33:51
```

Moonraker's current `metadata.py` recognizes any slicer writing that exact
shape:

```python
pattern = r"; generated by (.+?) on \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} at \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}"
```

then splits the capture on its last space into name and version. That path
("metadata: add support for unknown PrusaSlicer forks", commit `4637d70`,
2025-10-05) is **on master but not in any release yet** — it is after
v0.10.0. On a host new enough to have it, our files get a full card with
nothing installed and no patch: that is the whole reason the header carries
a timestamp, which is otherwise the only non-reproducible line in the file
(diff runs with `-I 'generated by'`).

No upstream change is needed. Adding "Fable Slicer" to the legacy alias
list would be redundant with the generic path — the maintainer added that
path precisely so unknown forks stop needing alias entries.

## Older hosts (v0.9.3, v0.10.0) — one line on the printer

These releases have no generic path, only a dict of known slicers, so they
report `"slicer": "Unknown"` and fall back to scanning `G1 Z` moves and
`M109`/`M190` — object height, first-layer height, two temperatures, and
nothing else.

`moonraker/components/file_manager/metadata.py`, in `PrusaSlicer.check_identity`:

```python
        aliases = {
            'PrusaSlicer': r"PrusaSlicer\s(.*)\son",
            'SuperSlicer': r"SuperSlicer\s(.*)\son",
            'OrcaSlicer': r"OrcaSlicer\s(.*)\son",
            ...
        }
```

Add one entry:

Idempotent, and it checks its own anchor before writing:

```bash
ssh <user>@<printer-host>
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path.home() / "moonraker/moonraker/components/file_manager/metadata.py"
src = p.read_text()
if "Fable Slicer" in src:
    print("already patched")
else:
    anchor = "        aliases = {\n"
    assert anchor in src, "anchor not found — check this Moonraker's metadata.py"
    entry = '            \'Fable Slicer\': r"Fable Slicer\\s(.*)\\son",\n'
    p.write_text(src.replace(anchor, anchor + entry, 1))
    print("patched")
PY
sudo systemctl restart moonraker
```

Re-scan a file (re-uploading also works) and check:

```bash
curl -X POST "http://<printer-host>:7125/server/files/metascan?filename=<file>.gcode"
curl "http://<printer-host>:7125/server/files/metadata?filename=<file>.gcode"
```

`"slicer": "Fable Slicer"` means it took. The patch does **not** survive
`moonraker update` — re-apply it, or wait for the release that carries the
generic path and drop the patch entirely.

## Verified

With the identity recognized, every field we emit parses on a real
Moonraker (v0.9.3, checked by temporarily swapping the name on a throwaway
copy): layer count, layer height, first layer height, object height,
estimated time, filament total mm, filament weight, filament type, filament
name, nozzle diameter, first-layer extruder/bed/chamber temperatures.

## Not done: thumbnails

Hosts read them as base64 PNG in the header:

```
; thumbnail begin 300x300 13600
; <base64 …>
; thumbnail end
```

That needs an isometric render (the GUI has an offscreen path) plus a real
PNG compressor — the minimal encoder in `gui/src/offscreen.rs` writes
uncompressed deflate, which would put roughly 480 KB of base64 at the top
of every file.
